decisions.rationale: Exhaustive comparison found no comparator with the reload UI's dev-session fallback disclosure, launch/status/log/error/termination lifecycle, and user-visible failure surface.
No comparator governs the non-normative use of external IDE affordances while retaining Puppet Master command, card, terminal, and authority semantics.
No comparator shares the terminal-specific quantitative workload, memory, responsiveness, throttling, platform, percentile, and failure-threshold acceptance boundary.
Tab and adjunct-session lifecycle gaps are plausible neighbors, but they do not own terminal reveal identity, replacement minting, disappearance races, or reveal-specific outcomes.
No comparator asserts the terminal-engine non-ship boundary requiring a purpose-built mutable grid core and forbidding document-style implementations.
Terminal/browser tab identity separation is adjacent, but it neither canonicalizes terminal command categories and aliases nor defines reveal targets by session identity.
Shared project-context propagation is downstream of project switching, but it is not the project-switch command-effect contract distinguishing replacement from opening a new workspace tab.
Both concern run termination guards, but exact repeated-error doom-loop detection has different triggers, lifecycle, state boundary, and failure semantics from first HTE tool observation termination.

These comparators preserve nearby Source Control, worktree, Orchestrator, and contradiction-evidence owner boundaries, but none has SMPFS-012's exact cross-owner split and consumed Orchestrator shell shape.
PTY stream delivery is one adjacent seam inside terminal architecture, not the full host/transport/grid/renderer/metadata/workspace layer contract.
No comparator defines or questions the hot-versus-live reload dev-session transition model, cleanup triggers, and cleanup-failure outcomes.
No comparator addresses the Run Modes contradiction between read-only Plan posture and prose describing plan execution in worktree context.

The classified outcome matrix is adjacent, but it concerns missing blocked-code closure rather than the exact budget-before/after, graceful-timeout, internal kill, and retired done.timeout refinements.
No comparator is the missing positive primary dev-loop model behind the stated non-goal, including its callers, transitions, and operational oracles.
Exact doom-loop termination is a neighboring guard, but shell-failure and write-thrash counters have different normalized identities, qualifying mutations, windows, exclusions, and resets.
PTY delivery semantics touch sensitive terminal channels, but do not own IME composition, grapheme indexing, keybinding precedence, locale fixtures, paste trust, or clear/cls behavior.
Tab lifecycle and missing terminal/tab recovery are plausible neighbors, but they do not define SMPFS-014's broad terminal-surface state transitions and scenario outcomes.
No comparator enumerates the terminal interaction-mode state space with valid/invalid combinations, ownership, and exit behavior.
Outcome-taxonomy closure is adjacent, but deferred-run liveness uniquely concerns wakeup ownership, backoff ceilings, prerequisite loss, offline posture, deadlock, and abandonment.
PTY stream delivery is a protocol neighbor, but it does not cover parser/screen fixture schemas, malformed input, negotiation, timeout/memory ceilings, and cross-platform executable protocol oracles.
Both expose outcome-mapping incompleteness, but the anchor is specifically the RM-016 budget-field-to-terminal-reason contract, while the comparator concerns a wider classified blocked-code matrix.
Adjunct-session restore is one resource-lifecycle neighbor, not the multi-resource workspace close transaction covering combined decisions, precedence, atomicity, and partial-close recovery.
Terminal/tabs recovery and PTY delivery are constituent seams, not the end-to-end terminal acceptance matrix spanning pane counts, dock states, identity, restore truth, linkbacks, and huge output.

Formatter delegation mentions DAE but has a formatter-chain lifecycle and file-mutation boundary; it is not DAE worktree/jail isolation, canonical-workspace non-writability, policy scans, and reconciliation.
PTY delivery is upstream adjacency; it does not share parser replay's grid, scrollback, anchor, annotation, reflow, Unicode, search, huge-output, and TUI correctness outcomes.
Generic event deduplication and PTY byte delivery are related infrastructure, but neither is the structured terminal pane/session lifecycle event surface and its named capability/error transitions.
The outcome matrix is adjacent, but the anchor is the specific contradiction assigning done.deferred both terminal paused-work and non-terminal waiting semantics.
Tab/session/stream identity concerns are neighbors, but SMPFS-015 uniquely assigns PTY identity minting and prohibits presentation or dev-session aliases from impersonating it.

The comparators cover Source Control ownership, File Manager handoff, and Source Control/Actions surfaces, but the anchor is a broader command-and-route coverage bundle including review, conflict, graph, history, and GitHub Actions pivots; umbrella and member structures remain distinct.
Search ownership and entrypoint conformance are adjacent, but neither defines the exact codesearch versus grep versus direct-LSP boundary with codesearch fallback tiers.

Removal/merge safety, recovery worktrees, binding actions, and merge/worktree control lifecycles are plausible neighbors or members; none matches the complete lineage-gated command lifecycle preserving repository, worktree, run, and orchestration truth across cleanup and rebinding.

Undo, exact revert, conflict lifecycle, hunk policy, and discard-hunk safety are members or adjacent controls. The anchor governs the broader destructive Source Control command family across revision races, idempotency, partial hunks, rollback, stale diffs, and receipts, so they are not merge-equivalent.

PF-0042 has the same Search-owner destructive multi-file replacement authority, replace-in-files/replace-all lifecycle, user outcome, stale-result and mutation state boundary, and partial-failure/undo/rollback semantics. Stale result opening and command-family separation are adjacent but distinct.

Actions compatibility routing is adjacent, but it does not embody the catalog contradiction that simultaneously marks cmd.actions.* compatibility-only and presents it as canonical without replacements, nor the duplicated canonical table.

These comparators cover broader remove/merge safety, worktree commands, worktree UI, mock authority, or lifecycle concurrency. The anchor is specifically the single confirmation policy for destructive removal across command and dropdown entry paths, so umbrella/member and adjacent concerns stay distinct.

The comparators are constituent handoff, file-tree, file/editor, or Source Control surfaces. They do not match the anchor's bundled wiring-verification hooks plus GitHub auth, project creation, file management, and LSP command families.

FileSafe application of semantic edits is a downstream safety seam, but the anchor concerns LSP mutator completion/failure events and recovery beyond invoked/denied, with different authority and lifecycle boundaries.

Runtime recovery worktrees, worktree UI commands, and Source Control/Orchestrator context are neighboring ownership slices; none matches the explicit project-scope versus assistant-thread authority split plus chat and Context Lens families.

Owner maps, worktree wrapper normalization, and Actions compatibility routing are related components, but the anchor bundles LSP/layout/runtime wrappers, Orchestrator metadata, external boundaries, namespace reservations, and aliases.
Search delegation, artifact opening, and runtime routing are members of the anchor's broader stable-owner routing bundle; their narrower lifecycles and failure semantics preclude merging.

The related worktree safety, recovery, binding, and control-lifecycle concerns do not include the anchor's combined atomic guard, stale-state, override audit, concurrent lifecycle, chat retention, and partial-failure rollback boundary.

Cross-worktree compare identity, File Manager handoff, compare-target choice, and GitHub account/compare binding are plausible neighbors. They have different owners or narrower boundaries and do not equal the Source Control review rule forbidding silent baseline substitution while exposing stale, missing, and blocked states.

Runtime recovery, concept binding actions, and merge/worktree controls overlap parts of the lifecycle. None establishes the same thread-scoped repository/worktree/path binding, frozen turn context, atomic consumer propagation, crash-safe creation/deletion, and recovery boundary.

Generic operation conflicts, hunk/conflict launch policy, canonical diff wiring, and discard-hunk safety are adjacent or member concerns. The anchor spans Git conflict resolution, merge-editor routing, mark-resolved/side-selection transitions, destructive content CAS, safe points, propagation, and rollback.

General Source Control operations and surfaces are umbrellas; neither shares commit-group acceptance and AI message generation with repository CAS, provider/model authority, privacy, prompt-injection resistance, and deterministic fallback.

The general Source Control surface contains graph/history as members, but does not match graph filter/focus/layout and commit-open navigation with alias identity, ordering, scale, virtualization, stale-object handling, and focus preservation.

GitHub Integration ownership, surface, and compare/account identity are adjacent, but none defines the provider-backed review open/filter/swap lifecycle with permissions, pagination, rate limits, force-push freshness, offline cache, and exact swap outcomes.

Tree clipboard, Save Local Copy, and overwrite/move safety are distinct members of the combined anchor. None alone shares its full clipboard lifecycle/privacy plus paste/save-copy durable mutation, validation, partial-failure, recovery, and projection-refresh boundary.

Canonical file-tree actions and the broad File Manager/editor contract are umbrellas. The anchor specifically owns create-file/create-folder/delete naming, collision, platform, content revision, confirmation, recoverability, atomicity, concurrency, cleanup, and success events.
